_format: One entry per good a basket may hold. `unit` is what quantities, silver prices and dollar prices are all counted in. `why` says what the good stands for and why a basket carries it (or the reason it was left out, for goods kept only for the playground). Sources and the full reasoning: specs/222-money-basket-and-section/research.md.

rice.name: Rice
rice.why: The staple, and the money: a koku is a mass of it.

soybeans.name: Soybeans
soybeans.why: Stands in for the miso, soy sauce, tofu and natto made from them.

beans.name: Beans
beans.why: Beans other than soybeans, such as adzuki.

barley-wheat.name: Barley and wheat
barley-wheat.why: The second grain of a commoner's bowl.

buckwheat-others.name: Buckwheat and millets
buckwheat-others.why: Buckwheat, foxtail, proso and barnyard millet, sorghum: the cheap grains.

cloth.name: Cloth
cloth.why: Cotton cloth for clothing, by the length of a Japanese bolt's width.

salt.name: Salt
salt.why: Needed to live, and to make miso, soy sauce and pickles.

fuel.name: Fuel
fuel.why: Firewood for cooking and heat: 3 million BTU a year, the usual allowance in historians' subsistence baskets.

housing.name: Housing
housing.why: A third of a small back-tenement room (about 10 m², 9 by 12 feet): one adult's share of a household's home.
